comment_text: I love this framing. Spatial reasoning has been underrated for so long.

post_text: LLMs are not enough. We need world models. Let me explain why current autoregressive approaches hit a ceiling...
comment_text: Interesting take. I'm not fully convinced but the world model argument is worth exploring.

post_text: We are closer to AGI than most people think. I want to be transparent about the challenges and responsibilities that come with that.
Stop calling everything AI. Most of what's labeled 'AI' in enterprise software today is just better search. Here's a taxonomy that actually helps...
comment_text: I love this breakdown. Sharing it with my whole team.

post_text: GPT-5 will not get us to AGI. Scaling alone has never been enough and never will be. The sooner we admit this, the sooner we make real progress.
comment_text: I'd argue the question isn't whether scaling is enough — it's whether the benchmarks we're using even measure what we think they measure. We might be solving the wrong problem entirely.

post_text: The path to solving protein folding has taught us that with the right problem formulation, AI can crack challenges that stumped scientists for decades.
comment_text: Brilliant work, no question. But I wonder if the real lesson is about problem formulation — and whether we're applying that same rigour to alignment. AlphaFold had a clear ground truth. Alignment doesn't.

post_text: Every company will be an AI company within 3 years. If you're not building AI into your core product today, you will not be competitive tomorrow. Full stop.
comment_text: I disagree. Plenty of businesses don't need AI at their core — they need reliable software, good operations, and trust. Forcing AI into everything is how you get bloated products and broken user experiences.

post_text: The AI safety debate is slowing us down. The bigger risk is falling behind in the global race. We need to move fast and figure out safety as we go.
comment_text: Respectfully disagree. 'Figure it out as we go' is exactly the mentality that has caused harm in social media. We already know what happens when you ship fast and patch later at scale. I don't think so.
